The naive recursive cofactor expansion has factorial growth, approximately
$$
O(n!).
$$

For
$$
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\qquad
B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p},
$$
the classical algorithm uses
$$
O(mnp)
$$
arithmetic operations. For dense square \(n\times n\) matrices, this becomes \(O(n^3)\).
Para \\(A\\in\\mathbb R^{m\\times n}\\):
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\ge n\), forming \(A^TA\) costs approximately
$$
O(mn^2),
